stem.en: The IUPAC name of CH₃COCH₂CH₃ is:

explanation.en: Four carbons with the C=O on C-2: butan-2-one (common name ethyl methyl ketone).

stem.en: The carbonyl carbon of aldehydes and ketones is:

explanation.en: The carbonyl carbon forms three σ bonds (sp²) in one plane about 120° apart; its unhybridised p orbital forms the π bond with oxygen.

stem.en: C₆H₅COCH₃ is commonly called:

explanation.en: A methyl phenyl ketone is acetophenone (IUPAC: 1-phenylethan-1-one). Benzophenone is C₆H₅COC₆H₅.

stem.en: How many structurally isomeric aldehydes and ketones have the formula C₄H₈O?

explanation.en: Butanal, 2-methylpropanal and butan-2-one: three carbonyl compounds.

solution.en: Butanal, 2-methylpropanal and butan-2-one: three carbonyl compounds.

stem.en: The carbonyl carbon is attacked by nucleophiles because:

options.en: It carries a partial negative charge
Oxygen is more electronegative, leaving the carbon electron-deficient (δ+)

explanation.en: The C=O bond is polarised towards oxygen; a resonance form C⁺–O⁻ contributes. The δ+ carbon is electrophilic and the δ− oxygen is nucleophilic/basic.

stem.en: Rosenmund reduction converts:

options.en: An acyl chloride into an aldehyde

explanation.en: R–COCl + H₂ → R–CHO + HCl over Pd on BaSO₄; the poisoned catalyst stops the reduction at the aldehyde stage.

stem.en: Ethyne is passed into dilute H₂SO₄ containing HgSO₄. The product is:

explanation.en: Water adds to the triple bond, giving the enol CH₂=CHOH, which tautomerises to ethanal. Other alkynes give ketones.

stem.en: In the Etard reaction, toluene is converted to benzaldehyde using:

explanation.en: Chromyl chloride oxidises the methyl group to a chromium complex, which is hydrolysed to benzaldehyde. KMnO₄ would go all the way to benzoic acid.

stem.en: Which of these compounds of similar molar mass has the highest boiling point?

explanation.en: Butan-1-ol forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds. Butanal has only dipole–dipole attractions, so it boils above the ether and alkane but below the alcohol.

solution.en: Butanal has only dipole–dipole attractions, so it boils above the ether and alkane but below the alcohol.

stem.en: Ethanenitrile (CH₃CN) is converted to ethanal by:

explanation.en: Stephen reaction: SnCl₂/HCl reduces the nitrile to an imine, which hydrolyses to the aldehyde. LiAlH₄, H₂/Ni and Na/ethanol all reduce nitriles to primary amines.

stem.en: Aldehydes are generally more reactive than ketones towards nucleophilic addition because:

options.en: Ketones have two alkyl groups that crowd the carbonyl carbon and reduce its positive charge

explanation.en: Two alkyl groups in ketones hinder the approach of a nucleophile (steric) and release electrons (+I), making the carbonyl carbon less electrophilic.

stem.en: Which of the following gives a silver mirror with Tollens’ reagent?

explanation.en: Aldehydes are easily oxidised; they reduce [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺ to metallic silver. Ketones and ethers do not.

stem.en: Clemmensen reduction converts a C=O group into a CH₂ group using:

explanation.en: Clemmensen uses zinc amalgam and concentrated HCl. Wolff–Kishner (hydrazine, then KOH in ethylene glycol) does the same job under basic conditions. NaBH₄ and LiAlH₄ give alcohols.

stem.en: Which of these does NOT undergo aldol condensation?

explanation.en: Aldol condensation needs an α-hydrogen. Methanal (HCHO) has none; with conc. alkali it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction instead.

solution.en: Methanal (HCHO) has none; with conc. alkali it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction instead.

stem.en: Which compound gives a positive iodoform test AND a positive Fehling’s test?

explanation.en: Ethanal has a CH₃CO– group (iodoform positive) and is an aliphatic aldehyde (reduces Fehling’s). Propanone fails Fehling’s; propanal lacks CH₃CO–; benzaldehyde fails both.

stem.en: The IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH is:

explanation.en: Four carbons including the carboxyl carbon (C-1): butanoic acid (common name butyric acid).

stem.en: Ethylbenzene is heated with alkaline KMnO₄ and then acidified. The product is:

explanation.en: Alkaline KMnO₄ oxidises any alkyl side chain that has a benzylic hydrogen down to –COOH, whatever its length, so benzoic acid forms.

stem.en: Carboxylic acids boil higher than alcohols of similar molar mass because they:

explanation.en: Two carboxyl groups hydrogen-bond to each other through two O–H···O bonds, forming dimers that persist even in the vapour phase.

stem.en: CH₃MgBr reacts with dry ice (solid CO₂), and the product is hydrolysed with dilute acid. The product is:

explanation.en: The Grignard carbon adds to CO₂: CH₃–COOMgBr, which acid hydrolysis converts to CH₃COOH. The acid has one carbon more than the alkyl halide.

solution.en: The Grignard carbon adds to CO₂: CH₃–COOMgBr, which acid hydrolysis converts to CH₃COOH.
The acid has one carbon more than the alkyl halide.

stem.en: Which of the following does NOT give a carboxylic acid on hydrolysis?

explanation.en: Nitriles, acyl chlorides and esters are acid derivatives and hydrolyse to acids. Methoxymethane is an ether and is not hydrolysed to an acid.

stem.en: Which is the strongest acid?

explanation.en: Electron-withdrawing halogens stabilise the carboxylate ion. Fluorine is the most electronegative, so CF₃COOH (pKa ≈ 0.23) is stronger than CCl₃COOH (≈ 0.65), ClCH₂COOH (≈ 2.86) and CH₃COOH (≈ 4.76).

stem.en: Which reagent distinguishes ethanoic acid from phenol?

explanation.en: Ethanoic acid (pKa 4.76) is strong enough to release CO₂ from sodium hydrogencarbonate (effervescence); phenol (pKa 10) is not. Both react with NaOH and with sodium.

stem.en: Sodium ethanoate heated with soda lime gives:

explanation.en: Decarboxylation: CH₃COONa + NaOH (CaO) → CH₄ + Na₂CO₃. The alkane has one carbon fewer than the acid.

stem.en: Propanoic acid is treated with Cl₂ in the presence of red phosphorus. The product is:

explanation.en: Hell–Volhard–Zelinsky reaction: carboxylic acids with α-hydrogens are halogenated at the α-carbon, giving 2-chloropropanoic acid.

solution.en: Hell–Volhard–Zelinsky reaction: carboxylic acids with α-hydrogens are halogenated at the α-carbon, giving 2-chloropropanoic acid.

stem.en: The correct order of acid strength is:

explanation.en: The –I effect of Cl weakens rapidly with distance. Nearest to –COOH (C-2) it stabilises the carboxylate most: pKa ≈ 2.9 (2-Cl), 4.1 (3-Cl), 4.5 (4-Cl), 4.8 (butanoic).

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Aldehydes are generally more reactive than ketones towards nucleophilic addition.
Reason (R): In ketones, two alkyl groups hinder the approach of the nucleophile and reduce the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon by their +I effect.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Both steric and electronic factors make the ketone carbonyl less reactive. R explains A.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Formic acid is a stronger acid than acetic acid.
Reason (R): The methyl group in acetic acid is an electron-withdrawing group.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: The CH₃ group is electron-donating (+I); it destabilises the acetate ion, so acetic acid is weaker than formic acid. A is true; R is false.

passage.en: A student is given two unlabelled liquids, M and N, both with molecular formula C₃H₆O and both containing a carbonyl group. On warming with Tollens' reagent, M forms a silver mirror while N does not. When N is warmed with iodine and sodium hydroxide, a yellow precipitate with a characteristic smell forms.

stem.en: Liquid N is:

explanation.en: N has a carbonyl group, does not reduce Tollens' reagent (not an aldehyde) and gives iodoform, so it has a CH₃CO– group: propanone (CH₃COCH₃).

passage.en: A student is given two unlabelled liquids, M and N, both with molecular formula C₃H₆O and both containing a carbonyl group. On warming with Tollens' reagent, M forms a silver mirror while N does not. When N is warmed with iodine and sodium hydroxide, a yellow precipitate with a characteristic smell forms.

stem.en: Which reagent would give a positive test with both M and N?

explanation.en: 2,4-DNP gives an orange-yellow precipitate with both aldehydes and ketones. Tollens' and Fehling's react only with the aldehyde M (propanal), and the iodoform test only with N.

stem.en: Which of the following give a positive iodoform test? One or more options may be correct.

explanation.en: The iodoform test needs a CH₃CO– group or a CH₃CH(OH)– group that can be oxidised to it. Ethanal (CH₃CHO) and propan-2-ol (CH₃CH(OH)CH₃) qualify; propanal (CH₃CH₂CHO) and pentan-3-one (C₂H₅COC₂H₅) do not.

stem.en: Which of the following undergo the Cannizzaro reaction with concentrated alkali? One or more options may be correct.

explanation.en: The Cannizzaro reaction needs an aldehyde with no α-hydrogen: HCHO, C₆H₅CHO and (CH₃)₃CCHO all qualify. Ethanal has α-hydrogens and gives the aldol reaction instead.

stem.en: 2.2 g of ethanal is warmed with excess Tollens’ reagent. What mass of silver (in g) is deposited? (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16, Ag = 108.) Give the answer to two decimal places.

explanation.en: Ethanal, CH₃CHO, has M = 44 g/mol, so 2.2 g = 0.05 mol. RCHO + 2[Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺ → RCOO⁻ + 2Ag, so 0.10 mol Ag = 10.80 g.

stem.en: Calculate the pH of a 0.01 M solution of ethanoic acid (Ka = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵), assuming the degree of ionisation is small. Give the answer to two decimal places.
Which of the following is the strongest acid?

explanation.en: Halogens withdraw electrons by the –I effect and stabilise the carboxylate ion. Fluorine is the most electronegative, so FCH₂COOH is the strongest acid here.

solution.en: Halogens withdraw electrons by the –I effect and stabilise the carboxylate ion.
Fluorine is the most electronegative, so FCH₂COOH is the strongest acid here.

stem.en: A carboxylic acid with an α-hydrogen is treated with Cl₂ and red phosphorus, then water. The product is:

options.en: A chloroalkane with one carbon fewer

explanation.en: This is the Hell–Volhard–Zelinsky reaction: the halogen replaces an α-hydrogen, giving R–CHCl–COOH.

stem.en: Which reagent converts propanone into propane?

explanation.en: Clemmensen reduction (Zn–Hg, conc. HCl) reduces >C=O all the way to >CH₂. NaBH₄, LiAlH₄ and H₂/Pd reduce propanone only to propan-2-ol.

solution.en: HCl) reduces >C=O all the way to >CH₂.
NaBH₄, LiAlH₄ and H₂/Pd reduce propanone only to propan-2-ol.

stem.en: An acyl chloride is converted into an aldehyde by hydrogen over palladium supported on barium sulphate (poisoned with sulphur / quinoline). This reaction is called:

explanation.en: Rosenmund reduction: RCOCl + H₂ → RCHO + HCl over Pd–BaSO₄. The catalyst is poisoned so the aldehyde is not reduced further to the alcohol. Stephen reaction starts from a nitrile.

stem.en: Ethanenitrile is reduced with SnCl₂ / HCl and the product is hydrolysed. The final product is:

explanation.en: Stephen reaction: RC≡N + SnCl₂/HCl → imine hydrochloride RCH=NH·HCl → H₃O⁺ → RCHO. So CH₃CN gives CH₃CHO. Complete reduction (LiAlH₄, Na/C₂H₅OH) would give ethanamine; hydrolysis without reduction gives ethanoic acid.

stem.en: Toluene is treated with chromyl chloride (CrO₂Cl₂) in CS₂ and the complex is hydrolysed. The product is:

explanation.en: Etard reaction: CrO₂Cl₂ oxidises the methyl group to a chromium complex that hydrolyses to C₆H₅CHO. Strong oxidants (KMnO₄) would take toluene all the way to benzoic acid.

stem.en: Which reagent distinguishes propanal from propanone?

explanation.en: Aldehydes are easily oxidised: propanal reduces ammoniacal AgNO₃ to a silver mirror; propanone does not. Both carbonyls react with 2,4-DNP, NH₂OH and NaHSO₃, so those cannot distinguish them.

stem.en: Which of the following does NOT give a red precipitate with Fehling's solution?

explanation.en: Fehling's test (Cu²⁺ → Cu₂O, red) is given by aliphatic aldehydes. Aromatic aldehydes such as benzaldehyde do not respond (though they do give Tollens' test).

stem.en: Acetophenone is heated with zinc amalgam and concentrated HCl. The product is:

explanation.en: Clemmensen reduction converts >C=O into >CH₂: C₆H₅COCH₃ → C₆H₅CH₂CH₃. Reduction to the alcohol (1-phenylethanol) needs NaBH₄ or LiAlH₄.

stem.en: The IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂–CO–CH(CH₃)₂ is:

explanation.en: Main chain: 5 C (CH₃CH₂–CO–CH–CH₃ with a CH₃ branch). Numbering from the branched end gives the C=O locant 3 and the methyl locant 2 (lower than 4) → 2-methylpentan-3-one. 'Ethyl isopropyl ketone' is the common name.

stem.en: Carboxylic acids boil higher than alcohols of comparable molar mass mainly because:

explanation.en: Two –COOH groups pair through two O–H···O=C hydrogen bonds (cyclic dimer). These bonds are stronger and more extensive than in alcohols and persist even in the vapour, so more energy is needed to vaporise the acid.

options.en: They are ionised in the liquid state
They exist as hydrogen-bonded dimers, even in the vapour phase

stem.en: Sodium ethanoate is heated with soda lime (NaOH + CaO). The gas evolved is:

explanation.en: Decarboxylation: RCOONa + NaOH → R–H + Na₂CO₃. The product has one carbon fewer: CH₃COONa → CH₄. Ethane would come from Kolbe electrolysis of sodium ethanoate.

stem.en: Ethanoic acid is treated with Cl₂ in the presence of a small amount of red phosphorus. This Hell–Volhard–Zelinsky reaction gives:

explanation.en: HVZ reaction halogenates the α-carbon of an acid having α-hydrogens: CH₃COOH → ClCH₂COOH (further Cl₂ gives di- and tri-chloroacetic acids). Ethanoyl chloride is made with PCl₅ or SOCl₂.

stem.en: Benzene is treated with CO and HCl in the presence of anhydrous AlCl₃ / CuCl. The product is:

explanation.en: Gattermann–Koch reaction: CO + HCl generate a formyl-cation equivalent (HCO⁺) that attacks the ring → C₆H₅CHO.

stem.en: Which reagent reduces ethanoic acid to ethanol?

explanation.en: Carboxylic acids are reduced to 1° alcohols by LiAlH₄ (or B₂H₆). NaBH₄ is too mild to reduce the –COOH group. Rosenmund's catalyst acts on acyl chlorides; Clemmensen acts on aldehydes/ketones.

stem.en: Which test is given by both aldehydes and ketones?

explanation.en: 2,4-DNP condenses with any >C=O to give a coloured 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone. Tollens', Fehling's and Schiff's tests depend on the easy oxidation (or specific reaction) of aldehydes and are negative for ketones.

stem.en: Bromoethane is converted into propanoic acid by the sequence:

explanation.en: C₂H₅MgBr adds to CO₂ to give C₂H₅COOMgBr, which is hydrolysed to C₂H₅COOH — one carbon more than the halide. Aq. KOH then KMnO₄ gives ethanoic acid (no extra carbon); HCHO gives propan-1-ol; KCN then H₂/Ni gives propan-1-amine.

options.en: Mg in dry ether, then CO₂, then H₃O⁺
Mg in dry ether, then HCHO, then H₃O⁺

stem.en: Benzoic acid and phenol can be distinguished by:

explanation.en: Carboxylic acids (pKa ≈ 4.2) are stronger than H₂CO₃ and liberate CO₂ (effervescence) with NaHCO₃; phenol (pKa ≈ 10) does not. Both dissolve in NaOH and both release H₂ with Na.

stem.en: 2.2 g of ethanal is warmed with excess Tollens' reagent. The mass of silver deposited (in g) is ____. (Ag = 108, C = 12, H = 1, O = 16) (in g)

explanation.en: RCHO + 2[Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺ + 3OH⁻ → RCOO⁻ + 2Ag + 2H₂O + 4NH₃. Moles CH₃CHO = 2.2/44 = 0.05 → Ag = 0.10 mol → 10.8 g.

stem.en: The correct order of reactivity towards nucleophilic addition (e.g. HCN) is:

explanation.en: Alkyl groups (+I) reduce the positive character of the carbonyl carbon and add steric hindrance, so HCHO (no alkyl) > CH₃CHO (one) > CH₃COCH₃ (two). In acetophenone the phenyl ring also conjugates with C=O (+R), lowering electrophilicity further → least reactive.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Benzaldehyde is less reactive than propanal towards nucleophilic addition.
Reason (R): The polarity of the carbonyl group in benzaldehyde is reduced by resonance with the benzene ring.

explanation.en: The ring donates electron density into the C=O by conjugation (C₆H₅–CH=O ↔ ⁺C₆H₅=CH–O⁻), so the carbonyl carbon is less electrophilic than in propanal. R correctly explains A.

options.en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

stem.en: Which compound will NOT undergo aldol condensation with dilute NaOH?

explanation.en: Aldol condensation requires at least one α-hydrogen to form the enolate. Benzaldehyde (C₆H₅CHO) has none; with conc. NaOH it undergoes Cannizzaro reaction instead. The other three all have α-H.

stem.en: Benzaldehyde is heated with concentrated NaOH. The products are:

explanation.en: Cannizzaro reaction (no α-H): one molecule is oxidised and one reduced by hydride transfer: 2C₆H₅CHO + NaOH → C₆H₅CH₂OH + C₆H₅COONa. Benzoin needs CN⁻ catalysis; cinnamaldehyde needs an aldehyde with α-H.

stem.en: An equimolar mixture of methanal and benzaldehyde is heated with concentrated NaOH. The main products are:

explanation.en: HCHO is the more reactive carbonyl, so OH⁻ adds to it and it becomes the hydride donor (is oxidised) → HCOO⁻Na⁺; benzaldehyde accepts the hydride (is reduced) → C₆H₅CH₂OH. This is why HCHO is used as a sacrificial reducing agent.

options.en: Sodium benzoate and benzyl alcohol only

stem.en: Benzaldehyde and acetophenone are warmed with dilute NaOH. The product of this Claisen–Schmidt condensation is:

explanation.en: Only acetophenone has α-H; its enolate attacks benzaldehyde, and the β-hydroxyketone dehydrates readily (the C=C is conjugated with both rings) → benzalacetophenone (chalcone), 1,3-diphenylprop-2-en-1-one. Option A is benzoin; D (cinnamaldehyde) would need ethanal.

stem.en: The correct order of acidic strength is:

explanation.en: Electron-withdrawing halogens (–I) stabilise the carboxylate; the effect follows electronegativity F > Cl > Br. pKa: FCH₂COOH 2.66, ClCH₂COOH 2.86, BrCH₂COOH 2.90, CH₃COOH 4.76.

stem.en: Arrange in decreasing order of acidity: methanoic acid, ethanoic acid, benzoic acid.

explanation.en: pKa: HCOOH 3.75, C₆H₅COOH 4.19, CH₃COOH 4.76. HCOOH has no electron-releasing group; the sp² phenyl carbon is mildly electron-withdrawing; CH₃ (+I) destabilises the acetate ion most.

stem.en: A ketone also contains an acid-sensitive acetal group. To convert its C=O into CH₂ without destroying the acetal, the best method is:

explanation.en: Wolff–Kishner works in strongly basic conditions (hydrazone → alkane + N₂), so acid-labile groups survive. Clemmensen needs hot conc. HCl, which would hydrolyse the acetal. NaBH₄ only gives the alcohol.

options.en: Wolff–Kishner reduction (NH₂NH₂, then KOH in ethylene glycol, heat)

stem.en:
Statement I: Reactions of aldehydes and ketones with ammonia derivatives (H₂N–Z) are carried out in weakly acidic medium (pH ≈ 3.5).
Statement II: In strongly acidic medium the nitrogen of H₂N–Z is protonated and loses its nucleophilicity, while in neutral medium the carbonyl is not activated.

explanation.en: Mild acid protonates the carbonyl oxygen (making carbon more electrophilic) yet leaves enough free H₂N–Z to attack. Too much acid converts the nucleophile into H₃N⁺–Z. Statement II is exactly the reason for Statement I.

options.en: Both statements are true and II is the correct explanation of I
Both statements are true but II is not the correct explanation of I
Statement I is true, Statement II is false
Statement I is false, Statement II is true

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Benzoic acid does not undergo Friedel–Crafts alkylation or acylation.
Reason (R): The –COOH group deactivates the ring and the AlCl₃ catalyst gets bonded to the carboxyl group.

explanation.en: –COOH is an electron-withdrawing, meta-directing deactivator, and the Lewis acid AlCl₃ complexes with its oxygen atoms, deactivating the ring further. Both are true and R explains A. (Benzoic acid can still be nitrated, giving m-nitrobenzoic acid.)

options.en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

stem.en:
Match the named reaction (List I) with the reagent used (List II).
List I: (P) Rosenmund reduction (Q) Stephen reaction (R) Etard reaction (S) Gattermann–Koch reaction
List II: (1) CrO₂Cl₂, then H₃O⁺ (2) CO + HCl, anhyd. AlCl₃ / CuCl (3) H₂, Pd–BaSO₄ (4) SnCl₂ + HCl, then H₃O⁺

explanation.en: Rosenmund: acyl chloride + H₂/Pd–BaSO₄ (3). Stephen: nitrile + SnCl₂/HCl (4). Etard: methylarene + chromyl chloride (1). Gattermann–Koch: arene + CO/HCl (2).

stem.en: An ester, CH₃CH₂COOC₂H₅, is to be converted into propanal in one step. The suitable reagent is:

explanation.en: Diisobutylaluminium hydride, (i-Bu)₂AlH, delivers one hydride and stops at the aldehyde stage when used cold, reducing esters (and nitriles) to aldehydes. LiAlH₄ goes on to propan-1-ol. NaBH₄ does not reduce esters readily; SnCl₂/HCl is for nitriles.

options.en: DIBAL-H at low temperature, then H₂O

stem.en: An aqueous solution of sodium propanoate is electrolysed (Kolbe's electrolysis). The hydrocarbon formed at the anode is:

explanation.en: At the anode RCOO⁻ → RCOO· → R· + CO₂, and two R· radicals couple: 2C₂H₅· → C₄H₁₀ (butane). H₂ is evolved at the cathode. Ethane would come from sodium ethanoate.

stem.en: The order of reactivity of carboxylic acid derivatives towards nucleophilic acyl substitution is:

explanation.en: Leaving-group ability Cl⁻ > RCOO⁻ > RO⁻ > NH₂⁻, and resonance donation of the substituent into C=O increases Cl < OCOR < OR < NH₂. So RCOCl > (RCO)₂O > RCOOR′ > RCONH₂.

stem.en: Propanoic acid is treated with Br₂ / red phosphorus and the product is then heated with excess ammonia. The final product is:

explanation.en: HVZ brominates the α-carbon: CH₃CH₂COOH → CH₃CHBrCOOH. Ammonia displaces bromide (SN2) → CH₃CH(NH₂)COOH, alanine. Propanamide would need the acid chloride + NH₃; 3-amino would need substitution at the β-carbon, which HVZ does not do.

stem.en: A compound C₈H₈O forms an orange precipitate with 2,4-DNP, gives a yellow precipitate with I₂/NaOH, does not reduce Tollens' reagent, and on vigorous oxidation gives benzoic acid. The compound is:

explanation.en: 2,4-DNP positive + Tollens negative → ketone. Iodoform → CH₃CO– group. Oxidation to benzoic acid → monosubstituted benzene ring. C₆H₅COCH₃ (C₈H₈O) fits. The other three are aldehydes (Tollens positive) and the methylbenzaldehydes would oxidise to phthalic/terephthalic acids.

stem.en:
How many of the following give a positive iodoform test?
CH₃CHO, CH₃COCH₃, C₆H₅COCH₃, CH₃CH₂COCH₂CH₃, HCHO, CH₃CH₂CHO, CH₃COCH₂CH₃, CH₃CH₂OH, CH₃COOH

explanation.en: Positive: CH₃CHO, CH₃COCH₃, C₆H₅COCH₃, CH₃COCH₂CH₃ (butanone), CH₃CH₂OH (oxidised to CH₃CHO) = 5. Negative: pentan-3-one, HCHO, propanal (no CH₃CO–), and ethanoic acid (its CH₃CO– is part of a resonance-stabilised –COOH, which is not halogenated under these conditions).

stem.en:
How many of the following reduce Tollens' reagent?
HCHO, CH₃CHO, C₆H₅CHO, HCOOH, CH₃COCH₃, CH₃COOH, C₆H₅COCH₃

explanation.en: All aldehydes — aliphatic and aromatic — give the silver mirror: HCHO, CH₃CHO, C₆H₅CHO. Methanoic acid (H–COOH) also contains an aldehyde-like H–C=O and is oxidised to CO₂. Ketones and ethanoic acid do not. Total = 4.

stem.en: 0.30 g of a monobasic carboxylic acid needs 25.0 mL of 0.20 M NaOH for complete neutralisation. The molar mass of the acid (in g mol⁻¹) is ____.

explanation.en: Moles NaOH = 0.025 × 0.20 = 0.005 mol = moles of monobasic acid. M = 0.30/0.005 = 60 g/mol → ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH.

stem.en: A mixture of ethanal and propanal is treated with dilute NaOH. Ignoring stereoisomers and dehydration, the number of different β-hydroxy aldehydes (aldol products) possible is ____.

explanation.en: Both have α-H, so each can be donor or acceptor: ethanal + ethanal, propanal + propanal, ethanal enolate + propanal, propanal enolate + ethanal → 2 self + 2 crossed = 4 aldols.

stem.en: The total number of structurally isomeric aldehydes and ketones with molecular formula C₅H₁₀O is ____.

explanation.en: Aldehydes (C₄H₉–CHO, four butyl groups): pentanal, 2-methylbutanal, 3-methylbutanal, 2,2-dimethylpropanal = 4. Ketones: pentan-2-one, pentan-3-one, 3-methylbutan-2-one = 3. Total = 7.

stem.en: Hexane-2,5-dione is heated with aqueous NaOH. The major product is:

explanation.en: Intramolecular aldol: the enolate at C-1 (terminal CH₃) attacks the C-5 carbonyl, forming a five-membered ring (C1–C5). Dehydration gives the conjugated enone; the ring carbon from C-5 carries the methyl and the C=C, so the product is 3-methylcyclopent-2-en-1-one. Attack from C-3 would form a strained three-membered ring. 2,5-Dimethylfuran forms only under acid (Paal–Knorr), not with NaOH.

stem.en: Arrange in decreasing order of acidity: (I) benzoic acid (II) 4-nitrobenzoic acid (III) 4-methylbenzoic acid (IV) 4-methoxybenzoic acid.

explanation.en: –NO₂ (–R, –I) stabilises the benzoate → strongest (pKa 3.41). Benzoic acid 4.19. –CH₃ (+I/hyperconjugation) 4.36. –OCH₃ at para is a strong +R donor → weakest (4.47). So II > I > III > IV.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): 2-Methylbenzoic acid is a stronger acid than benzoic acid, although –CH₃ is electron-releasing.
Reason (R): The ortho substituent twists the –COOH out of the plane of the ring, reducing resonance between ring and carboxyl (the 'ortho effect').

explanation.en: pKa: o-toluic acid 3.91 vs benzoic acid 4.19. Almost every ortho substituent raises benzoic acid's acidity. Steric inhibition of resonance stops the ring from donating electrons into the carboxyl group, and that stabilises the carboxylate relative to the acid. R explains A.

options.en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

stem.en: Glyoxal (OHC–CHO) is heated with concentrated NaOH and then acidified. The product is:

explanation.en: Glyoxal has no α-H, so it undergoes an intramolecular Cannizzaro reaction: OH⁻ adds to one CHO, which transfers a hydride to the other CHO in the same molecule. One end is oxidised to –COO⁻ and the other reduced to –CH₂OH → HOCH₂COO⁻ → glycolic acid on acidification.

options.en: A 1 : 1 mixture of oxalic acid and ethane-1,2-diol

stem.en: Semicarbazide (H₂N–NH–CO–NH₂) reacts with a ketone through only one of its NH₂ groups. The semicarbazone formed is:

explanation.en: The –NH₂ attached directly to C=O is an amide nitrogen; its lone pair is delocalised onto oxygen, so it is weakly nucleophilic. The terminal –NH₂ of the hydrazine part (–NH–NH₂) is free and attacks → R₂C=N–NH–CO–NH₂.

stem.en: Benzene is acylated with succinic anhydride / AlCl₃ to give X. X is reduced with Zn-Hg / HCl to Y, and Y is heated with conc. H₂SO₄ (or H₃PO₄) to give Z. Z is:

explanation.en: X = C₆H₅CO–CH₂CH₂–COOH (Friedel–Crafts acylation). Clemmensen reduces only the ketone: Y = C₆H₅CH₂CH₂CH₂COOH. Strong acid then makes the –COOH attack the ring ortho to the chain (intramolecular acylation), closing a six-membered ring → α-tetralone (Haworth synthesis; further reduction / dehydrogenation leads to naphthalene). Options A and B are Y and X.

stem.en: On ignition, 0.458 g of the silver salt of a monobasic organic acid leaves 0.216 g of metallic silver. The molar mass of the acid (in g mol⁻¹) is ____. (Ag = 108)

explanation.en: Moles Ag = 0.216/108 = 0.002 = moles of RCOOAg. M(salt) = 0.458/0.002 = 229. The acid RCOOH has H in place of Ag: 229 − 108 + 1 = 122 → benzoic acid. A common slip is reporting 229 or forgetting to add back the H (121).

stem.en: Which reagents convert cyclohexanone directly into cyclohexane?

explanation.en: Clemmensen (acidic) and Wolff–Kishner (basic) both reduce >C=O to >CH₂. NaBH₄ and LiAlH₄ stop at the alcohol (cyclohexanol).

options.en: NH₂NH₂, then KOH in ethylene glycol at 453 K

stem.en: Which of the following give a positive test with BOTH Tollens' reagent and Fehling's solution?

explanation.en: Aliphatic aldehydes give both tests. Methanoic acid (H–COOH) is a reducing agent and reduces both Tollens' and Fehling's reagents (oxidised to CO₂). Benzaldehyde gives Tollens' but not Fehling's. Propanone gives neither.

stem.en: Which aldehydes undergo the Cannizzaro reaction with concentrated NaOH?

explanation.en: Cannizzaro needs an aldehyde without α-hydrogen. HCHO, (CH₃)₃C–CHO and C₆H₅CHO qualify. Propanal has α-H and undergoes aldol condensation instead.

stem.en: Which statements about carboxylic acids are correct?

explanation.en: A true: the –OH lone pair is delocalised into C=O, so typical carbonyl addition reactions do not occur. B true. C false: NaBH₄ does not reduce acids. D false: carboxylic acids (pKa ≈ 4–5) are much stronger than phenol (pKa ≈ 10) because the carboxylate charge is shared equally by two oxygens.

options.en: They do not form oximes or 2,4-DNP derivatives, because resonance in –COOH lowers the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon
NaBH₄ reduces RCOOH to RCH₂OH in methanol
They are weaker acids than phenol
